findings.evidence: quotientProdEquiv_symm_apply_mk's body never mentions quotientProdInvMap; Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot exists at mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Quotient/Basic.lean:236, and the removed Fredholm proof (diff, `refine LinearEquiv.ofBijective g ⟨?_, ?_⟩`) is 8 lines.
findings.fix: Define quotientProdEquiv := LinearEquiv.ofBijective (quotientProdMap p q) ⟨_, _⟩, with injectivity from LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mp (Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot _ _ h.ge h.le) and surjectivity by `rintro ⟨⟨x⟩, ⟨y⟩⟩` — the proof this PR deleted from Analysis/Fredholm/Prod.lean. Both public simp lemmas survive unchanged; delete lines 52-115.
findings.issue: Lines 52-115 (quotientProdInlMap, quotientProdInrMap, quotientProdInvMap, quotientProdInvMap_apply_mk/_inl/_inr, and both comp-is-id lemmas) exist only to supply an explicit inverse to LinearEquiv.ofLinearMap. No proof uses that inverse definitionally: quotientProdEquiv_symm_apply_mk (line 141-142) goes through LinearEquiv.symm_apply_eq and the forward lemma, which works for any equiv. Six of these are private @[simp] lemmas that still enter the global simp set under unnameable names.

findings.evidence: Lines 99-102 and 108-115: six `case ... => simp [LinearMap.comp_apply]` branches with identical bodies.
findings.fix: Replace each proof body with `ext x <;> simp`; the case split carries no information since all branches are the same tactic.
findings.issue: quotientProdInvMap_comp_quotientProdMap (98-102) and quotientProdMap_comp_quotientProdInvMap (107-115) select goals by ext-generated case labels (`case hl`, `case hr`, `case hl.fst`, `case hl.snd`, `case hr.fst`, `case hr.snd`) while giving every branch the identical tactic. Those labels are binder names in Mathlib's @[ext] lemmas and break on any rename or reordering upstream.

findings.evidence: Line 76-77: `rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_add]` then `congr 1; simp` to prove `(x, 0) + (0, y) = (x, y)`.
findings.fix: Close with `simp` (or `simp [Prod.ext_iff]`) after the mk_add rewrite instead of `congr 1`, or drop the lemma entirely per the previous finding.
findings.issue: quotientProdInvMap_apply_mk closes with `rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_add]; congr 1; simp`. `congr 1` on a quotient-mk equality is brittle: it can peel the Quotient.mk congruence differently after an instance or definition change, leaving an unrelated goal for the trailing `simp`.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Span/Basic.lean:391-393 (`Submodule.mem_prod := Set.mem_prod`); OrthogonalSum.lean:95 (`orthogonalSum_carrier := (rfl)`); OrthogonalSum.lean:73 uses `Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier` successfully.
findings.fix: Define `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv := Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier` and, if any downstream `rfl` proof does fail, prove it from `Submodule.prodEquiv_apply`/`prodEquiv_symm_apply` rather than from defeq. If a genuine obstruction exists, name the declaration whose proof breaks instead of a general claim about instance terms.
findings.issue: The new docstring justifies re-inlining the equivalence with "Reusing `Submodule.prodEquiv` introduces different instance terms and loses the definitional computation rules below". The obstruction is asserted, not demonstrated, and the surrounding evidence contradicts it: `Submodule.mem_prod` is `Set.mem_prod` (`Iff.rfl`), so `(Submodule.mem_prod.mp p.2).1` is defeq to `p.2.1`, and `orthogonalSum_carrier` is `(rfl)`, so the two equivs' toFun/invFun and module instances agree definitionally. Line 73 already applies `Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier` at exactly this type.

summary: The new quotientProdEquiv is built through ~64 lines of private inverse-map scaffolding that no proof in the file actually uses, replacing the short LinearEquiv.ofBijective proof the PR deleted. Two proofs also address brittle ext-generated case names, and the OrthogonalSum docstring asserts an unverified definitional-equality obstruction to reuse.
